period_scope: French Third Republic; core concession 1883–1893, with later survivor attribution recorded in 1950
granting_body: French Republic; awarded by the President on proposal of the competent War or Navy ministry

legal_records.instrument: Chamber of Deputies debate / adopted proposal
legal_records.official_reference: J.O. 19 June 1885, Débats parlementaires, Chambre, p. 1134
legal_records.effect: Proposal for a commemorative medal for the China and Tonkin expedition; the page preserves the debated wording, not the final physical type.
Created the silver 30 mm medal for operations against China and Annam in 1883–1885; initial ribbon half green and half yellow; President grants on ministry proposal.
Warned that privately sold Tonkin medals and ribbons were not regulatory; only officially delivered pieces could be worn.
Applied the listed disciplinary rules to Tonkin-medal holders.
Specified replacement ribbon for non-commissioned officers and soldiers: 36 mm, silk, green and jonquil-yellow stripes.

Extended eligibility after 1886 to effective operations in Tonkin/Annam, Cambodia and Madagascar, and covered earlier service with Francis Garnier and operations from 1873–1883; surviving-family delivery rules included.
Explained delivery to families of deceased eligible soldiers.

legal_records.official_reference: Bulletin Officiel de l’administration des Colonies, 1893, no. 7, p. 558
legal_records.effect: Stated that rights to obtain the Tonkin medal ceased from 1 October 1893, subject to the page’s discussion of 1893 operations.
Recorded a later attribution to ex-corporal Jean-François Roux; this is not a new model or new period of general concession.

date_conflicts.handling: Retain both statements; use 26 July 1887 for the transcribed law record and flag the one-day page-narrative discrepancy.

eligibility_summary: The page states 1883–1885 expedition service, then extension to operations in Tonkin, Annam, Cambodia, Siam and Haut-Mékong in 1885–1893, plus surviving participants under Francis Garnier and Henri Rivière for 1873–1882. It records 97,300 holders and diploma delivery; no exact individual issue date is inferred from that total.
physical_description: Round silver medal, 30 mm, engraved by Jean-Baptiste Daniel Dupuis. Obverse: helmeted Republic, REPUBLIQUE FRANÇAISE, PATRIE on the visor, laurel surround. Reverse: TONKIN CHINE ANNAM • 1883-1885 • with battle names within a laurel wreath. The 10 April 1886 Mint note says the official type carries a Corne d’abondance mark under the central battle inscription and that this guarantees 950/1000 fineness.

scope: French Colonial Medal; Tonkin clasp section of the SAMLHOC Colonial Medal page and its official-text compilation
period_scope: French Third Republic and later continuation of the Colonial Medal; Tonkin clasp eligibility from 1893 onward
granting_body: French Republic; military and naval personnel, with listed civil/indigenous eligibility in particular decrees
base_medal_basis: SAMLHOC states the Colonial Medal was created by Article 75 of the finance law of 26 July 1893, is a 30 mm silver medal with Republic obverse and globe/military attributes on reverse, suspended from a white-and-blue striped ribbon, and receives one clasp for each possession in which rights were earned. It became Médaille d’Outre-mer under decree 62-660 of 6 June 1962.
related_page_section: SAMLHOC medaille_coloniale page, TONKIN section lines 1188–1226 in the captured page; official-text compilation lines 284–333 and 2396–2448.

legal_records.official_reference: SAMLHOC Colonial Medal history; law creating the medal
legal_records.effect: Created the Colonial Medal; Tonkin clasp is a later campaign variant of this same family.

legal_records.official_reference: J.O. 10 June 1895, p. 3237; SAMLHOC official-text compilation
legal_records.effect: Created the Tonkin clasp for effective war operations in Tonkin or Annam from 1 October 1893; the page also explains the earlier Tonkin medal had ceased from that date.

legal_records.official_reference: Journal Militaire, 1895, second semester, p. 193; related 30 September 1895 circular
legal_records.effect: Confirmed that holders of the pre-1 October 1893 Tonkin medal who later took part in new Tonkin operations could receive the Colonial Medal.
Tonkin clasp for effective war operations at Kouang-Tchéou-Wan from 22 April 1898.
Tonkin clasp for personnel of the 1901 mission laying the Amoy–Tourane cable landings.
Tonkin clasp for operations against the Kiem band in Hoa-Binh, 4 August 1909–2 January 1910.
Tonkin clasp for Son La/Sop-Nao/Muong-Hou-Tai/Muong-Boum-Neua operations, Ban-Phong-Sek on 11 August 1915, and specified Haut-Laos/Lai Chau operations in 1915–1916.

Tonkin clasp for Thai-Nguyen operations, 1 September 1917–20 January 1918; also qualifying 12-month service in the 4th and 5th military territories in 1917–1918, with wound/citation exceptions and listed civil personnel.
Tonkin clasp for operations in the Tonkin military territory and Quang-Yen province, 16 November 1918–20 June 1919.
Tonkin clasp for repression of the Meos revolt, 1 September 1919–1 April 1920.

Tonkin clasp for naval personnel in the Tonkin military territory and Quang-Yen, 16 November 1918–20 June 1919; SAMLHOC lists Quentin-Roosevelt, Torpilleurs 18 S/21 S and 19 S/20 S with service dates.
Tonkin clasp for operations against Chinese pirates in Lang Son province, 26 January–24 February 1914.
Tonkin clasp for Haut-Laos operations, Lang Son–Cao Bang fighting 9–22 October 1921, and Tien Hoi operations 5–7 January 1922.
Tonkin clasp for operations in the first Tonkin military territory, Bac Phong Sinh region, 6–12 April 1922.
Tonkin clasp for Hoan-Mo on 8 February 1927, Nam-Si on 19 November 1927, and qualifying six-month service in the first Tonkin military territory during 1927.
Tonkin clasp for effective operations by the Trung-Khanh-Phu garrison, 1 February–15 May 1928; partisan eligibility could follow a special report for wounds or distinction.

campaign_clasps: Tonkin — created 7 June 1895; subsequent eligibility expansions: Kouang-Tchéou-Wan; Amoy–Tourane cable mission; Hoa-Binh/Kiem; Son La and Haut-Laos/Lai Chau; Thai-Nguyen; Tonkin/Quang-Yen 1918–1919; Meos revolt; Lang Son; Haut-Laos/Lang Son–Cao Bang/Tien Hoi; Bac Phong Sinh; Hoan-Mo/Nam-Si and 1927 service; Trung-Khanh-Phu.

legal_records.instrument: Arrêté no. 367 creating the Médaille du Mérite
legal_records.official_reference: Bulletin Officiel de l’Indo-Chine française, 1890, second part, p. 714
legal_records.effect: Created a decoration for indigenous troops or civil guards of the Annam and Tonkin protectorate for serious wounds or conspicuous military action; annual allowance twelve piastres; register kept at Hué and Hanoi.

legal_records.official_reference: Bulletin Officiel de l’Indo-Chine française, 1890, second part, p. 972
legal_records.effect: Awarded the medal to Nguyen-van-Hang of the 1st Tonkinese Tirailleurs for an action on 4 July 1890 near Tien-son; the page records this as the only named recipient.
Paris instruction preceding repeal of the creation order.

Reported the 21 July 1890 order; existing holders provisionally retained associated rights. The page’s preamble contains a 19 July 1890 date typo, while the title/history and signed text use 21 July 1890.

physical_description: Round silver medal, partly gilded, 30 mm. Ribbon 36 mm: yellow with 6 mm blue edging and two black Đông-Khánh ideograms vertically woven at the centre. Obverse central medallion carries eleven Chinese ideograms and a surrounding oak/laurel wreath. Reverse carries VALEUR ET DISCIPLINE and PROTECTORAT DE L’ANNAM ET DU TONKIN. A fixed dragon head/claw suspension touches the wreath, with the ring fixed to two crossed Chinese dāo sabres. SAMLHOC attributes manufacture to Maison Lasne in Paris, now Maison Bacqueville.
eligibility_summary: Restricted to indigenous troops or civil guards of the Annam and Tonkin protectorate, only for serious wounds or conspicuous action; no numbered classes are stated.
